text: max_ease is applied by the COMPILER, not only by the runtime, and a config whose ease is greater than or equal to its dwell is refused by name. THE DEFECT IS SPLIT ENFORCEMENT, NOT AN UNLUCKY PAIR OF CONSTANTS -- cc's correction, verified from source f593de8: showreel:799-800 applies min_dwell and min_ease and NEVER applies max_ease, while the cap lives only in player.html's easeOf, at the Math.min(..., LIM.max_ease) token -- cited by token because 3903937 moved it off the line this row named until 2026-09-09, whereas the two showreel citations here were swept the same day and are correct, and showreel:988 comments 'the runtime enforces the same floors' when it enforces one the compiler does not have. One limit, two homes, disagreeing, and a comment asserting a parity that does not hold -- this thread's own dominant class, in the code about to be ported. README section 7's claim that compiler and player both enforce the floors is false for max_ease. hv RULED 2026-09-09: max_ease is capped at 2400. That is ONE constant and it closes the whole crossing space STRUCTURALLY rather than by refusal -- runtime ease <= 2400 < 2500 <= runtime dwell, for every config, every speed and both pace modes. vc verified the envelope in source before putting it up: cc was right that no compile-time enforcement closes it, because at ?speed=16 a config with dwell 20000 and ease 2600 crosses while authored ease sits eight times under authored dwell, so the compiler cannot see it. What the measurement added is that BOTH defects -- the constants crossing at speed=1, and the dwellOf/easeOf asymmetry crossing at any speed -- reduce to one condition, runtime ease exceeding the 2500 dwell floor. Capping below that floor makes it unreachable rather than refused, which is the difference between a guard and a rule. Cost: no reel may crossfade slower than 2.4s; 45h's worst authored ease is 900, so nothing real moves. Raising min_dwell instead would also work and was not taken, because it changes pacing for every existing slide.

state.evidence: VERIFIED BY vc AT THE SOURCE. The three constants read from limits.rs: MIN_DWELL_MS 2500, MIN_EASE_MS 600, MAX_EASE_MS 2400 -- hv's cap, against the reference's 3000 which exceeded min_dwell and was the second defect. timing() returns Timing { dwell_ms: dwell_ms.max(MIN_DWELL_MS), ease_ms: ease_ms.clamp(MIN_EASE_MS, MAX_EASE_MS) }, so THE COMPILER APPLIES max_ease WHERE THE REFERENCE NEVER DID -- the reference applied min_dwell and min_ease and left the cap to player.html's easeOf alone, which is the split enforcement this row was minted about. The ease >= dwell case returns a Failure naming the segment and BOTH durations, with a remedy explaining that ease is the crossfade inside the dwell rather than an addition to it. AND THE SUBTLE HALF IS BUILT AND PROVED: the refusal reads the AUTHORED values rather than the clamped ones, and clamping_can_never_manufacture_the_violation proves by cases that a pair which is sound before clamping cannot become unsound after it -- so the two mechanisms cannot disagree, which is the property that makes checking the authored values safe rather than merely convenient.
